the pulsations in the metre–wave radiation received from certain flares may be attributed to modulation of the radiation by MHD waves set up within a flux tube embedded in a coronal cloud and that energetic protons, as well as electrons, may be accelerated by a similar process.
“The pulsations of the type IV radio emission are produced by the interaction between the solar wind and the coronal magnetic field.”
the solar radio emission from a solar flare is modulated at the same frequency as the solar wind.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.

the study of the physical processes involved in the acceleration of energetic particles in the solar corone and their subsequent escape into interplanetary space, where they may cause geomagnetic storms.
the origin of solar cosmic rays, and the pulsations which are observed in the radio emission from some large solar flares are a key element in the proposed acceleration process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a flare of sufficient magnitude and energy can generate a magnetic flux tube in which electrons can be accelerated to relativistic energies by the mechanism of first-order Fermi acceleration and in which they can emit synchrotron continuum radiation which is modulated by MHD waves.
the pulsating type IV continuum is the radio manifestation of a solar flare in which a magnetic flux tube is involved.

the phenomenon of pulsating continuum radiation from the Sun is a manifestation of the interaction between the solar wind and the solar atmosphere, which results in the acceleration of charged particles to relativistic energies and in the generation of MHD waves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the pulsations are a real phenomenon and not an artefact of the recording system, and we have presented evidence that the pulsations can be attributed to MHD waves propagating in a magnetic flux-tube in the solar coronal region.
solar cosmic rays may be generated in the corona, not by shock waves as is usually thought, but by MHD waves, and that this process may be observed in the radio continuum.
solar cosmic rays may be generated by a process similar to that by which the Sun's corona is heated to a temperature of 106 K.
